subtitle: The first ARPANET Data Management meeting, August 2-3, 1971.

tldr.problem: Different ARPANET sites were thinking about how computers on the network should handle shared data, but there was no coordinated effort or common understanding.
tldr.mechanism: Leaders from IBM, SDC, University of Utah, MITRE, Harvard, and CCA organized a two-day meeting for researchers to present different approaches to network data management and exchange ideas.
tldr.outcome: The meeting brought together the early thinking on network databases, data sharing, and data management protocols that would influence later ARPANET standards.

today: This RFC is an announcement of an early data management meeting from 1971. It reflects the nascent thinking about shared databases on the ARPANET and represents efforts to coordinate network research communities around critical problems.

sections.title: A New Challenge
sections.content:
In 1971, ARPANET researchers were beginning to think seriously about data management and data sharing across the network. Different research groups had different ideas about how network data should be organized, accessed, and managed. To bring the community together, researchers from MITRE and IBM organized the first Network Data Management meeting.

The meeting was hosted by Richard Winter at the Computer Corporation of America and held in Cambridge, Massachusetts on August 2 and 3, 1971. It was designed to let people exchange ideas and develop a working data management group with both formal paper presentations and informal discussions.
sections.plainLanguage: Scientists at different computer centers needed to figure out how to share information across the network. They met in Boston to share their ideas.

sections.title: Topics and Speakers
sections.content:
Monday morning addressed three different philosophical approaches: A. Shoshani from SDC presented three approaches to data sharing, B. Wessler from University of Utah described a Unified Data Management System, and P. Karp from MITRE offered a data management overview.

Monday afternoon covered language considerations, including discussions of data definition languages (DDL), the Codasyl database model report, and how data should be accessed and arranged. Tuesday morning featured presentations on the Data Computer project at CCA and plans for its use. The agenda concluded with a planning session to decide on next steps for network data management standardization.
sections.plainLanguage: Presenters talked about different ways to organize data, how to describe it, and how computers could share it across the network.

sections.title: Meeting Logistics
sections.content:
The meeting was held at 545 Technology Square in Room 801 in Cambridge, Massachusetts. A block of rooms was reserved at the Sonesta Hotel (5 Cambridge Parkway, Cambridge). The document provided directions from Logan Airport (approximately four dollars by taxi) and a rough map showing the hotel's location off Route 1 and Technology Square's location on Main Street about half a mile away.

The RFC references earlier RFCs on related topics (144, 146, 171, 172, 173, and 195) and notes that some papers would be distributed with the original announcement.
sections.plainLanguage: The meeting was in a building in Cambridge, with hotel rooms nearby. Directions and a map were provided so people knew where to go.

references.text: Karp, P. M., McKay, D. B., "Data Management Meeting Announcement", RFC 188, January 1971.
